scope: ARMHF and AArch64 Linux ELFs built for new public multi-device releases
method: Each item is closed by repository-owned policy, implementation and deterministic host gates. Historical approved binaries are audited report-only and do not become release-eligible merely because they are useful loader references.

guarantees: ARMHF GCC and Clang plus the AArch64 container image and sysroots are versioned or hash pinned
the release-facing toolchain command fails when an exact pin is unavailable
residual_scope: historical non-hermetic recipes are read-only evidence and cannot produce a new public artifact
tests: mutate a compiler version, sysroot hash or image digest and require the gate to fail

guarantees: GLIBC 2.17 is the preferred public floor
owned libm fixtures bind the oldest viable exported symbols instead of accepting a 2.27 floor silently
residual_scope: an approved historical binary is not rebuilt solely to lower its floor; touching it requires new bytes and physical revalidation
tests: build with and without nx_symver and verify the preferred-floor warning disappears only for the pinned variant

guarantees: GLIBC 2.30 is an absolute ceiling for a public universal profile
private and unsupported GLIBC tokens fail independently of the numeric ceiling
residual_scope: a lower per-release ceiling may be requested, never a higher one
tests: inject GLIBC 2.31 and GLIBC_PRIVATE fixtures and require errors

guarantees: nextos-current is a named non-public profile
a current-glibc artifact cannot silently enter the universal-low-glibc package path
residual_scope: a NextOS-only artifact is separate output and never satisfies a public universal release gate
tests: label a current-host ELF as universal and require rejection

guarantees: inventory discovers every ELF under declared files and directories
an ELF hidden in generic payload is rejected as unclassified
residual_scope: only allowlisted stage inputs are in scope; undeclared host files are neither copied nor audited as package members
tests: place an auxiliary ELF below a payload directory and require fail-closed classification

guarantees: Android-namespace BYO ELFs are identified separately and never counted as Linux builds
an Android-tagged ELF that imports GLIBC is rejected
residual_scope: redistribution eligibility is an M18 package concern, separate from M17 ABI classification
tests: audit Android linker and Linux linker fixtures with crossed namespaces

guarantees: ELF class, endianness, machine and ARM EABI hard-float flags are checked against the declared architecture
residual_scope: Android ARM soft-float calling conventions remain loader/adapter contracts and are not relabelled as Linux ARMHF
tests: mutate class, endian, machine and float flags independently

guarantees: at least one PT_LOAD is mandatory
PT_INTERP is unique, absolute and exact for the ABI; executable stacks are rejected or reported
residual_scope: static ELFs may legitimately omit PT_INTERP but still require a loadable ELF type and PT_LOAD
tests: exercise missing PT_LOAD, duplicate or wrong PT_INTERP and executable GNU stack

guarantees: DT_NEEDED and SONAME multiplicity are checked
public universal ELFs reject RPATH and RUNPATH and audit dependency names against policy
residual_scope: the approved Horizon artifact keeps its historical RUNPATH error and is never a packaging reference
tests: inject duplicate DT_NEEDED, noncanonical SONAME, RPATH and RUNPATH

guarantees: GLIBC, GLIBCXX and CXXABI maxima are extracted and compared with policy ceilings
GLIBC_PRIVATE and ABI-only tokens fail
residual_scope: unversioned third-party ABI compatibility still requires its dependency contract and target acceptance
tests: audit independent over-ceiling GLIBCXX and CXXABI fixtures

guarantees: SDL, OpenAL and every auxiliary Linux ELF are subject to the same recursive inventory and dependency policy
development-symlink SONAMEs are rejected for new builds
residual_scope: firmware availability is still a declared dependency-provider contract rather than an invented bundled library
tests: package an auxiliary SDL or OpenAL library above the ceiling and require the whole release to fail

guarantees: GCC 8.2.1 ARMHF compiler and its sysroot files are pinned by version and SHA-256
residual_scope: a historical script that downloads another compiler is outside the closed toolchain path
tests: verify the compiler banner and each pinned sysroot hash

guarantees: the supported ARMHF Clang target, sysroot, GCC toolchain and linker flags are explicit
residual_scope: host Clang without the pinned target/sysroot flags is not a public artifact compiler
tests: compile the same contract with GCC and Clang and reject missing hard-float or linker flags

guarantees: SDL 2.0.4 is the explicit symbol floor
symbols introduced later fail unless an exact historical artifact waiver records the limitation
residual_scope: a waiver never applies to rebuilt bytes and never changes the default floor
tests: import a post-2.0.4 SDL symbol and mutate a waived artifact hash

guarantees: newer libc/POSIX wrapper imports are machine-audited against a finite blacklist
wrappers through the public GLIBC 2.30 ceiling remain visible warnings while wrappers introduced later fail and direct the target to a syscall or project shim
residual_scope: a null-version review entry is informational until policy can prove an introduction version
tests: audit memfd_create as a warning, close_range as an error and a safe legacy wrapper without a finding

guarantees: inventory JSON records hashes, ELF headers, segments, dynamic tags, version ceilings and toolchain notes
audit JSON records deterministic findings and counts
residual_scope: reference reports omit embedded inventory by design; release inventories embed every packaged ELF
tests: round-trip the JSON schema and reject missing or duplicated facts

guarantees: any public ELF above GLIBC, GLIBCXX or CXXABI ceilings produces a failing exit status
nxrelease repeats the audit on the final package
residual_scope: report-only approved references may contain recorded errors but cannot pass as new release artifacts
tests: add one over-ceiling auxiliary ELF among otherwise clean files and require release failure

guarantees: every inventory record carries SHA-256 and build-id when present
owned builds embed a toolchain provenance note derived from the pin
residual_scope: missing notes on historical approved bytes remain warnings and do not authorize their reuse in a fresh public package
tests: strip ordinary comments and verify the project toolchain note remains recoverable

guarantees: owned ARMHF and AArch64 fixtures are each built twice in distinct temporary trees
the AArch64 build runs in the exact pinned image with networking disabled and all declared artifacts must have identical SHA-256
residual_scope: each actual port recipe must use the same gate when it starts producing new release bytes
tests: embed a build path or current timestamp and require the double-build comparison to fail

guarantees: one fail-closed gate verifies pins, units, deterministic build, owned-fixture ABI and the exact sanitized reference receipt
the checked-in report contains only approved relative paths and one documented non-packaging error
residual_scope: M17 closure covers the framework and new public artifacts; it does not rewrite or falsely certify historical approved binaries
tests: run the closure validator and the complete nx-abi-gate from a clean temporary work tree
